Subject: OrionEdge access cutover — initial sequencing and prereqs

Hi Olivia / OrionEdge IT team,

Thanks again for partnering with Redwood — excited to get the access controls cutover scheduled. To make the implementation low-risk we want to confirm a minimal, ordered sequence and collect the environment artifacts so our eng team can provision and validate ahead of the dry run.

Proposed high-level sequencing (rough):
1) SAML/Sso test in your staging tenant (metadata exchange + 1 test user)
2) SCIM provisioning: map 4 core attrs, run a limited group sync (staging)
3) IP allowlist: establish CIDR ranges for staging then prod; confirm NAT/public IPs
4) Service accounts: create named service principal(s) for Redwood canary and for provisioning; apply least privilege roles
5) Production cutover: rolling switch with health-checks and rollback gate

Can you share the following artifacts by EOD Tue so we can preconfigure?
- Tenant ID and SAML metadata (staging + prod)
- SCIM base URL and token for staging (we recommend scoped token)
- Public IP ranges for testing and prod outbound
- Any org policies that will block service principals or custom app registrations

I attached a checklist (orionedge-onboard-prereqs.xlsx) and a short service account checklist. If you prefer a quick 30-min technical sync tomorrow we can invite our infra lead (Jordan) and the implementation PM (Ben).

Thanks — Naomi

--

Thanks for the details — helpful. A few notes from the implementation side and suggested sequencing that reduces blast radius:

1) SAML in staging: Redwood will perform metadata import and SSO smoke (login + logout + attribute assertion). We want one test user in the "redwood-testers" group; Amit, can you confirm the group name and membership?
2) SCIM mapping: we'll initially map displayName, mail, uid, and department. We'll run a push test for 10 users in staging — if that looks good we'll expand to the pilot group.
3) IP allowlist: recommend we apply staging CIDR to a Redwood staging endpoint first; only after SAML/SCIM pass do we extend to prod endpoints.
4) Service accounts: two principals — redwood-provisioner@orionedge (used for SCIM writes) and redwood-canary@orionedge (used for health checks). We need an Azure AD owner to grant "Application.ReadWrite.OwnedBy" for the provisioner; list that owner during the sync.

Rollout gating logic: 0 critical errors in SAML assertions, SCIM sync with <1% error on the selected 10 accounts, canary health checks stable for 30 minutes.

I'll bring a short runbook to the Wed sync and we can lock the dry-run window.

—Jordan
